 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda
 M.A.C.M.A. No.585 of 2020
Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the appellant-petitioner being not satisfied with the award and decree dated 05.02.2019 passed in M.V.O.P.No.573 of 2013 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VII Additional District Judge, Nizamabad (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VII Additional District Judge, Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner sustained injuries in the road accident, has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 r/w Rule 455 of the A.P Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, against the respondents to pay a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation together with the interest @ 24%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization against which the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,30,038/- towards compensation payable to the petitioner with future interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Being not satisfied with the said award and aggrieved by the same appellant-petitioner preferred present appeal on the ground that the learned Tribunal did not chose to consider the huge medical expenditure incurred for the treatment and NNRJ granted meager amount of compensation.

It is also contended that appellant was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years at the time of accident and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month but the learned Tribunal did not chose to award any compensation under the head Loss of Earnings.

Though, it is contended that the appellant sustained fracture injuries in the accident and having sustained grievous injuries and could not attend his normal duties and the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded the compensation under the head of loss of earnings, future loss of earnings, attendant charges and future medical expenses.
3.
It is submitted that respondent No.1 was set ex parte before the Tribunal as such notice on respondent No.1 is dispensed with.

4. Heard learned counsel for the appellant-petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5.

Having heard and on perusing the entire material placed on record including the record from the lower Court, the point that arose before this Court is that "whether the appellant- petitioner is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?".
NNRJ 6.

The main grievance of the petitioner before this Court is that the appellant has sustained grievous injuries like fracture of Nasal Bone, fracture of right thigh, fracture of skull, fracture of ribs and other multiple injuries all over his body but as per the injury certificate, it is submitted that petitioner sustained only nasal injury and injury on thigh.

Admittedly, petitioner was shifted to Surya Hospital, Armoor, where he was given treatment and referred to Government Head Quarters Gitta Ravi , Jitta Ravi vs Mrs. Venkata Lakshmi Madicharla And ... on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115379597/
1 Hospital, Nizamabad from there he was referred to Hyderabad for expert and specialist treatment.

entities.text: Gitta Ravi , Jitta Ravi vs Mrs. Venkata Lakshmi Madicharla
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He was admitted in Care Hospital, Hyderabad where he was treated as inpatient from 30.04.2012 to 12.05.2012.
7.

It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the learned Tribunal did not considered the aspect of loss of earnings, loss of future earnings and also the attendant charges for the purpose of assessment of loss of earnings, the petitioner ought to have examined any of the doctor to show that the nature of the treatment obtained by the petitioner and the advise given by the said doctor and also the bed rest obtained by the petitioner.

Besides that the petitioner did not chose to place any evidence before the Tribunal to show the income proof even NNRJ otherwise as the contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner was driver and doing vegetable business and considering the age of the petitioner he might have earn some amounts by way of doing driver occupation and doing the vegetable business, but nothing has been placed before the Tribunal.
But considering the ground realities the income of the petitioner can be taken into consideration as Rs.5,000/- per month which an ordinary agricultural labourer would get.
Considering the same and also the treatment obtained by the petitioner as per the record and considering the probable issues, the petitioner might have taken bed rest for about two to three months.
Considering the same, an amount of Rs.15,000/-ought to have been awarded by the learned Tribunal, but in the present case the learned Tribunal has lost sight about the same.

Besides that the learned counsel for the petitioner has also sought for the compensation towards future loss of earnings which the learned Tribunal did not chose to award the same for the reason that no disability certificate was produced by the petitioner as such I do not see any ground to interfere in respect of the said finding.
NNRJ 8.
As further seen from the record, that learned Tribunal was pleased to award an amount of Rs.2,15,038 towards the medical expenses.

Basing on the medical bill which is submitted by the petitioner before the Tribunal and the learned Tribunal was also kind enough to award an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards transportation charges, Rs.15,000/- towards two injuries sustained by the petitioner and Rs.15,000/- towards pain and suffering for the two injuries and also ought to have award an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards extra nourishment.

As the petitioner has no grievance as to awarding of the said amount, but the only aspect which the petitioner raised before this Court is in respect of above three heads i.e., loss of earnings during the treatment obtained, loss of attendant charges and loss of future earnings for which the petitioner having not placed any disability certificate and also not placed any evidence to show that attendant was engaged, in absence of evidence to that extent the same cannot be awarded.

9. Coming to the aspect of loss of earnings during the treatment, as held by this Court in the earlier paragraphs, the petitioner would be entitled for an amount of Rs.15,000/- in addition to the compensation which was already granted under NNRJ the same head loss of earnings during the period of treatment.

Therefore, the amount of enhanced compensation comes to Rs.3,45,038/-
(Rs.3,30,038 + Rs.15,000/-).

sentences.text: In the result, appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation of Rs.3,30,038 granted by the learned Tribunal to Rs.3,45,038/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the said amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment after deducting the amount if any already deposited.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw the said amount.
No costs.
